claims.text: Tested large language models repeat or elaborate on fabricated medical details in 50% to 82% of cases under default prompting.
Prompt-based mitigation lowers the mean hallucination rate across all tested models from 66% to 44% (p < 0.001).
For GPT-4o, prompt-based mitigation reduces hallucination rates from 53% to 23% (p < 0.001).
Setting decoding temperature to 0 does not produce a statistically significant reduction in LLM hallucination rates.
Short clinical vignettes show higher odds of hallucination compared to long clinical vignettes (OR = 1.22, p = 0.003).
Distilled-DeepSeek exhibited the highest hallucination rates among tested models under default settings (80.0% in long cases and 82.7% in short cases).
GPT-4o exhibited the lowest hallucination rate among tested models under default settings (53.3% for long cases and 50.0% for short cases).

evidence.description: Hallucination rates range from 50 % to 82 % across models and prompting methods.
Prompt-based mitigation lowers the overall hallucination rate (mean across all models) from 66 % to 44 % (p < 0.001).
For the best-performing model, GPT-4o, rates decline from 53 % to 23 % (p < 0.001).
Temperature adjustments offer no significant improvement (the zero-temperature condition had an OR of 1.05, 95% CI 0.89–1.23; p = 0.58).
Short-format cases had an OR of 1.22 (1.07–1.39; p = 0.003) compared to long-format cases.
Under default configuration settings, Distilled-DeepSeek had the highest hallucination rates (80.0% in long cases and 82.7% in short cases).
GPT4o had the lowest hallucination rates (53.3% for long cases and 50.0% for short cases).

methodologies.name: Adversarial clinical hallucination evaluation framework
methodologies.description: A systematic evaluation framework generating 5,400 outputs across six LLMs using 300 physician-validated clinical vignettes containing embedded fabricated details tested under default, mitigation prompt, and zero-temperature settings.

limitations.text: The evaluation relied on simulated clinical vignettes rather than real-world clinical data, which may not fully capture authentic clinical practice.
Only six LLMs under three specific experimental conditions were tested, excluding other available models and system configurations.
Each prompt sample was run only once per experimental condition, which may under-represent run-to-run stochastic variability.
The study did not evaluate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or external search lookup mechanisms.
Black-box reasoning processes make it difficult to determine how LLM outputs are produced, leading to fabricated references or facts.

future_work.text: Repeat each sample prompt across multiple stochastic draws to tighten uncertainty bounds.
Broaden model comparisons, test retrieval-augmented generation methods, and evaluate narrowly constructed domain-specific clinical LLMs.
